newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude outrights remain weak, grades even.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude outrights remain weak, grades even.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes remained weak in Monday afternoon trade, maintaining losses established from session's open on news the United Nations finalized an aid distribution plan with Iraq.

Optimistic projections place the return of Iraqi crude liftings from late next week, but most traders expect first liftings in early August, and any shipments to U.S. destinations landing in September.

The market took on a bearish tone after Iraq hit screens, pushing benchmark August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing below $19.00 a barrel. Outrights recovered slightly but still remained around that level later in the day.

Cash dealers confirmed a low number of deals in what was termed a cold grade market. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was dealt at 20 and 21 cents over the August benchmark, with Midland/WTI barrels done at 27 cents under WTI.

Sour deals were steady at $1.31 and #1.32 below benchmark for West Texas Sour/Midland parcels. The looming return of Iraqi crude failed to jostle WTS, partially due to support from force majeure declarations on Colombian Cano Limon barrels following the bombing of pipelines by rebels.
Other deals had WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold at $1.82, $1.83 and $1.86, against a Aug/Sep roll of minus 17 cents.
